name: Database Management Systems
topics: DBMS Concepts, Architecture and DBA
Explain the three-level schema architecture and logical/physical data independence.
Why use a DBMS over a file system? Give DBMS functions and applications, design anomalies, and the role of a DBA.
Keys and Integrity Constraints
Differentiate super, candidate, primary, composite and alternate keys with examples.
Explain referential integrity and the significance of integrity constraints.
ER Modelling and Mapping to Relations
Draw an ER diagram for the given scenario (music company / hospital / university academics / projects–clients) with all constraints.
Differentiate strong and weak entity sets; explain specialisation/generalisation and ternary relationships; map the ER diagram to relations.
SQL Queries
Write SQL queries on the given schema (flights/aircraft/employees, customer/vehicle/rental, employee/department).
Explain GROUP BY, views, DROP vs DELETE, COMMIT vs ROLLBACK, and inner vs outer join with examples.
Relational Algebra
Write relational algebra expressions for the given queries on the Sailors–Boats–Reserves / Customer–Vehicle–Rental schema.
Convert the given SQL to relational algebra; express cross product via join; differentiate selection and projection; when are relations union-compatible?
Functional Dependencies and Normalisation
For the given relation and FDs, find the closure, candidate keys and normalise to 2NF/3NF/BCNF.
Why is normalisation needed? Differentiate 3NF and BCNF; explain lossless-join decomposition and transitive dependency.
Transactions, ACID and Serializability
Explain ACID properties and the transaction state diagram.
Explain serial vs non-serial schedules and conflict serializability with examples; explain dirty read and other concurrency problems.
Concurrency Control, Locking and Deadlocks
Explain two-phase locking and strict 2PL with benefits and drawbacks.
What is deadlock? Illustrate with three transactions and explain a prevention scheme.
Advanced Databases: Distributed, Multimedia, Object-Oriented
Explain the framework of a distributed DBMS and fragmentation.
Write notes on multimedia databases; distinguish relational and object-oriented data models.
